examples.ko: 고속철을 타면 서울에서 부산까지 세 시간이 안 걸려요.
examples.en: By high-speed rail, it takes under three hours from Seoul to Busan.
A new high-speed railway will open next year.
China's high-speed rail network is really long.

examples.ko: 우리 지역에도 고속철 역이 생겼으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope a high-speed rail station is built in our area too.
Thanks to high-speed rail, business trips became much easier.

examples.ko: 고속철보다 비행기가 더 빠를 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes a plane is faster than high-speed rail.

explain: 고속철은 '고속철도'를 줄인 말로 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 나와요. 한국에서는 일상에서 'KTX'라고 하는 사람이 훨씬 많아요. 외국의 같은 열차를 말할 때는 '고속철'을 쓰는 편이에요.
explain_en: 고속철 is short for '고속철도' and appears often in news. In daily life in Korea, many more people say 'KTX'. For similar trains in other countries, 고속철 is more common.

examples.en: The police detained the criminal.
I feel like the promise is binding me.
He tries to control his partner and calls it love.
The court decides whether to detain that person.
If you restrict a child too much, the child feels stifled.
I hope rules don't tie people down.

explain: 뉴스에서는 경찰이나 법원이 사람을 잡아 가둘 때 써요. 일상에서는 자유롭게 못 하게 묶는다는 뜻으로 써요. 명사 '구속'도 두 경우에 모두 써요.
explain_en: In the news it means police or courts detaining someone. In daily life it means tying someone down so they lack freedom. The noun '구속' covers both.

en: no matter how long; for ages

examples.ko: 백날 말해도 그 사람은 안 들어요.
examples.en: No matter how long you tell him, he won't listen.

examples.ko: 백날 연습만 하면 뭐 해요, 실전에서 못 하면요.
examples.en: What's the use of practicing forever if you can't do it in the real thing?

examples.ko: 백날 기다려 봐야 연락은 안 올 거예요.
examples.en: You can wait all you want, but no call will come.
Crying like that for ages won't help at all.

examples.ko: 백날 부탁해 봐야 안 된다고 할 거예요.
examples.en: No matter how often you ask, they'll say no.

examples.ko: 이렇게 앉아만 있으면 백날 해도 안 끝나요.
examples.en: If you just sit here like this, it won't be finished no matter how long you go on.

explain: 실제로 백 일을 말하는 게 아니라 '아무리 오래 해도'라는 느낌으로 써요. 뒤에 '~어도, ~아 봐야'와 함께 안 된다, 소용없다는 말이 오는 때가 많아요. 불만이나 답답함을 나타내는 구어 표현이에요.
explain_en: It does not literally mean a hundred days; it carries the feel of 'no matter how long you do it'. It often comes with '~어도' or '~아 봐야' followed by a negative result such as 'it won't work' or 'it's useless'. It is a spoken expression that conveys frustration or exasperation.

examples.en: Is it okay if I sit right here?

examples.ko: 요기에 놓아 둔 가방 못 봤어요?
examples.en: Did you see the bag I left right here?
My house is a five-minute walk from right here.
The child pointed and said it was right here.
Let's stop right here and take a break.
There's a tasty bakery right around here.

explain: '여기'를 가볍고 귀엽게 말할 때 써요. 친구나 아이에게 말하듯 편한 말투라서 윗사람이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '여기'가 안전해요. 같은 소리의 '요기하다'(조금 먹다)와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: This is a light, cute way to say 여기. It sounds like talking to friends or children, so with elders or in formal settings 여기 is the safe choice. Don't confuse it with 요기하다, which has the same sound but means to eat a little.

p.n: 여기 is neutral; 요기 sounds playful and points to a nearer spot.
